For example, a translating step can produce a corner in interval mass when its jump crosses an endpoint, so a finite-time balance does not imply classical time differentiability at every time.

rationale: The translation preserves the real scalar setting, transport formula, speed, unchanged shape, flux orientation, and distinction between characteristic derivatives and classical coordinate derivatives. Its added geometric clauses follow from the displayed profile formula and do not introduce uniqueness. Acceptance remains unresolved because the supplied evidence does not determine the integration measure, the intended nonsmooth profile class, or the precise temporal meaning of the source conservation law. These gaps require adjudication rather than inferred equivalence or a definitive mismatch.
